key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN workflow can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify process windows that minimize defects.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical welding guidelines showing that bottom preheating and higher rotational speed can stabilize forces, increase temperature uniformity, and improve weldability.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of FSW in HDPE
Validated against experimental thermal, force, and defect observations
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained to predict temperature and axial force responses
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved high predictive accuracy with reported R2 values from 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched experiments for void formation and thermo-mechanical responses.
watch_item: The process maps are based on the tested HDPE parameter range, so performance outside the studied speeds and preheating conditions may not generalize.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
